chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about ghusl of janabah. He said: Pour water over your hands and wash your palms, then put your hand into the water and wash your private part, then rinse your mouth and inhale water into your nose, and pour water over your head three times, and wash your face, and let the water flow over your body. The implication here is that we understand this as recommended rather than obligatory, so that the reports do not conflict.

key_terms.تَتَمَضْمَضُ: you rinse the mouth during purification
key_terms.تَسْتَنْشِقُ: you draw water into the nose during purification
key_terms.جَسَدِكَ: your body, over which water is made to flow in ghusl
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, over which water is poured in ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah

ai.seo_question: In ghusl al-janabah, are rinsing the mouth and inhaling water into the nose obligatory or recommended?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the procedure of ghusl for janabah, including washing the hands, private part, rinsing the mouth, inhaling water into the nose, pouring water over the head, washing the face, and flowing water over the body. The final phrase indicates that the mention of rinsing the mouth and nose is to be understood as recommended rather than obligatory in order to reconcile the narrations.
